Launching a medical‑device app in both the United Kingdom and Germany requires compliance with two distinct regulatory regimes that, while convergent in many respects, are governed by separate statutory frameworks. In the European Union, the Medical Device Regulation (EU 2017/745) has been superseded for new devices by the updated MDR 2024 provisions that became fully effective on 26 May 2024. Under this regulation, the app must be classified according to its intended purpose and risk profile, and a conformity‑assessment procedure must be undertaken with an authorised Notified Body if it falls into Class I (sterile or non‑sterile), Class IIa, IIb, or III. The manufacturer is required to compile a technical file that includes a clinical evaluation, post‑market surveillance plan, and risk management documentation in accordance with Annex II and Annex III of the MDR. The Notified Body will issue a CE marking certificate only after verifying compliance with all applicable essential requirements.

In the United Kingdom, the UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (as amended) provide for the UKCA marking, which is currently considered equivalent to the CE mark for devices that are also marketed in the EU. However, post‑Brexit regulatory oversight has been transferred to the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA). The app must therefore obtain a UKCA mark through either self‑certification (for Class I) or a conformity assessment by an authorised body (for higher classes). In addition, NHS Digital’s App Marketplace imposes its own set of requirements: the app must pass the NHS Digital Digital Health App Assessment Framework, demonstrating compliance with data security standards, interoperability (e.g., FHIR), and user‑experience guidelines. The NHS also requires that any health‑related data be stored in accordance with the NHS Information Governance Toolkit, which may necessitate local hosting or a UK‑based data centre.

**Data‑Protection Compliance**

Both jurisdictions are bound by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) as applied within the EU and by the UK GDPR together with the Data Protection Act 2018. The app will process personal health information, which is classified as “special category data” under Article 9 of the GDPR and the UK DPA. Consequently, a lawful basis such as explicit consent or legitimate interest must be established, and a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is mandatory for high‑risk processing activities. In Germany, the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) supplements the GDPR with stricter provisions on health data, including mandatory data minimisation and specific rules governing cross‑border transfers of medical information. Because the app will be available in both jurisdictions, any transfer of personal data from the EU to the UK must rely either on the European Commission’s adequacy decision (which may have been revised post‑2024) or on Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the Information Commissioner’s Office. The manufacturer should also consider appointing a Data Protection Officer and implementing robust technical measures such as encryption, pseudonymisation, and secure authentication to satisfy both GDPR and BDSG requirements.

**Contractual Considerations**

The commercial architecture of the app will involve multiple contractual layers: agreements with device manufacturers or developers, distribution contracts in Germany (often governed by German Commercial Code provisions), NHS procurement contracts (which may be subject to the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and NHS Digital’s own procurement policies), and reimbursement arrangements that could trigger German HTA processes. The contracts should contain clear clauses on liability, indemnity, warranties, and product liability insurance that reflect the differing tort regimes in the UK and Germany. Data‑sharing agreements with NHS Digital or German health authorities must incorporate GDPR/BDSG compliance clauses, including obligations to report breaches within 72 hours and to provide audit rights. An 18‑month launch window is ambitious but attainable with a disciplined project plan.
